title: Dravid and Sehwag's Sons Open India's U-19 Asia Cup Campaign Against Nepal
excerpt: Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag are in India's 15-man squad, led by Lakshya Raichandani, for the ACC Men's U-19 Asia Cup opener in Muscat on Friday.
body:
• India open their ACC Men's U-19 Asia Cup campaign against Nepal on Friday, November 6, at the Oman Cricket Academy Turf 1 in Muscat, starting 10:30 a.m. IST.
  • The 15-man squad is captained by Lakshya Raichandani, with Yashbardhan Singh Chauhan as vice-captain, the BCCI announced on October 30.
  • Wicketkeeper Anvay Dravid and batter Aaryavir Sehwag — sons of Rahul Dravid and Virender Sehwag — are both in the squad and drew the pre-match spotlight.
  • India are in Group A with Nepal, Pakistan and the UAE; the final is on Saturday, November 14.

India's Under-19 campaign begins with two famous surnames on the team sheet. Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag take centre stage as India face Nepal in their opening Group A match of the ACC Men's U-19 Asia Cup in Muscat on Friday, NDTV Sports reported in its match coverage.

The squad and the tournament

The Junior Cricket Committee picked a 15-man squad for the tournament, to be played in Muscat, Oman, from November 5 to 14, the BCCI announced. Lakshya Raichandani captains the side, with Yashbardhan Singh Chauhan as vice-captain. The full squad: Lakshya Raichandani (captain), Aaryavir Sehwag, V.K. Vineeth, Yashbardhan Singh Chauhan, Kushagra Ojha, Arjun Rajput, Manal Chauhan, Anvay Dravid (wicketkeeper), Rajat Baghel (wicketkeeper), V. Yashveer, Aryan Savsani, Mohit Ulva, Kavya Patel, Shavin Vinod and Ishan Sood.

India are placed in Group A alongside the UAE, Nepal and Pakistan. Their first fixture, against Nepal, is listed by the BCCI for Friday, November 6 at OCC Turf 1, Muscat, and Cricbuzz lists the match at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground (Ministry Turf 1), starting 9:00 a.m. local time, 10:30 a.m. IST. Nepal are captained by Bipin Sharma, with Aashish Luhar as wicketkeeper.

The Nepal side, and the wider draw

Nepal's squad for the match, as listed by Cricbuzz, is: Bipin Sharma (captain), Aashish Luhar (wicketkeeper), Niraj Kumar Yadav, Rohit Chand, Prashiddha Jaishi, Sohail Kunwar, Darsh Sonar, Nischal Chhetri, Sachin Bhatt, Roshan Shahi, Suryanshu Koirala, Abhay Yadav, Sushil Rawal, Subham Khanal and Nitesh Patel. The tournament's Group B contains Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Sri Lanka, so the two group winners' paths cross only from the knockout stage. For India, that structure makes the group games against Pakistan and the UAE — not the Nepal opener — the fixtures most likely to decide how hard their route to the November 14 final becomes.

Why this opener matters

For India, the Nepal game is the softest entry into a group that also contains Pakistan — the fixture that will decide the group's top seed. For Dravid and Sehwag, it is a first tournament outing under the weight of two of Indian cricket's most recognisable names, in a format where India have historically been the strongest side. The final takes place on Saturday, November 14. No result is in yet: this is a preview, and the scorecard will tell whether the surnames, or the captain, make the first headline of the tournament.
